output.reason: A 68-year-old with two weeks of worsening bilateral ankle swelling and new orthopnea over the last two nights suggests decompensating heart failure needing immediate emergency assessment with oxygen saturation, imaging and bloodwork that messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Worsening swelling in both ankles plus needing to sit up to breathe the last two nights can mean fluid backing up from a failing heart, and that needs same-hour oxygen checks, a chest image and blood tests. Have someone drive you. If you become severely breathless, get chest pain, or faint, call 911 immediately.
differential: Decompensated heart failure with pulmonary congestion
Other volume-overload cause (kidney or liver disease)
